text: Lemma N1 [on paper]. $J_k=\mathrm{span}\{\mu(r)-1:r\in R_0\}+\sum_j\big(J_{k-1}a_j+a_jJ_{k-1}\big)$, the products taken in $A_k$ (also modulo $2^E$). Proof. For $z\in J_{k-1}$ take a lift $\tilde z\in J_k$; $\tilde z a_j=za_j$ in $A_k$ because the degree-$(k-1)$ part of $\tilde z$ dies in the product; so "$\supseteq$". Conversely $J_k$ is spanned by $u(\mu(r)-1)v$ with monomials $u,v$; if $v=v'a_j$, then $u(\mu(r)-1)v=\big(u(\mu(r)-1)v'\big)a_j$ and the bracket is in $J_k$, its truncation in $J_{k-1}$; the same on the left. $\square$

Each step is a congruence modulo $J_k$ ($u-\mathrm{NF}_{k-1}(u)$ is the truncation of an element of $J_k$; the difference is in degree $k-1$ and dies after the shift) and moves to strictly later columns; $\pi_k$ is the result. So $x-\pi_k(x)\in J_k$, $\pi_k$ is the identity on $C_k$, and $$x\in J_k\iff\pi_k(x)\in\pi_k(J_k),\qquad A_k^+/J_k\cong\mathbb Z^{C_k}/\pi_k(J_k)$$ — the index, the free columns and generators are those of the dense form, so the certificate of §6.4 applies unchanged.

otin S_{k-1}$ with $u[{:}{-1}]\in S_{k-1}$ and $a_j\,u[{:}{-1}]
otin S_{k-1}$. Proof. By N1, with the generating set $\{g_u=u-\mathrm{NF}_{k-1}(u):u
otin S_{k-1}\}\cup\{	ext{torsion rows}\}$ of $J_{k-1}$ (the reduced Howell form in all columns). $\pi_k(g_ua_j)=0$ by the prefix rule. $\pi_k(a_jg_u)=0$ when $a_j u[{:}{-1}]\in S_{k-1}$ (the suffix rule applies to $a_ju$). If $u=u'a_l$ with $u'
otin S_{k-1}$: $z=g_u-g_{u'}a_l\in J_{k-1}$ lies on columns after $u$, and $a_jg_u= ig(a_jg_{u'} ig)a_l+a_jz$ in $A_k$; the first term is a right shift of an element of $J_{k-1}$ (its $\pi_k$ is in the span of (ii)), and $z$ is a combination of $g_x$, $x>u$, and torsion rows (Howell property); induction downwards on $u$. $\square$
